first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and these memories indicate that simplifying or shortening onboarding improved completion, time-to-value, and early activation. Verify durability and downstream revenue quality before committing, because the inherited evidence does not directly establish long-term qualified revenue impact.

mid.rationale: Run a standard guarded simplification experiment focused on self-serve SMB accounts. The verified evidence directly addresses both current declines: signup simplification raised activation 9% and qualified revenue 4%, while shortened onboarding raised completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention 3%. Maintain retention and qualified-revenue guardrails because signup simplification previously reduced 30-day retention 1% and its result was not replicated beyond SMB.

final2.rationale: Pivot this cycle’s experiment to tightly targeted promotional pricing for price-sensitive SMB accounts. The competitor’s deeper cut and doubled churn conversations make price the most acute qualified-revenue risk, while inherited evidence indicates targeted pricing can lift acquisition and revenue in this segment. Keep the test small and time-bound with retention, margin, qualified-revenue, and post-promotion churn guardrails because memory_73 could not be source-verified this cycle and does not establish long-term effects.
